title: ECB Governing Council Holds Key Interest Rates Steady Amid Disinflation Progress
text:
The European Central Bank's Governing Council decided at its September monetary policy meeting to leave the three key ECB interest rates unchanged. The deposit facility rate remains at 3.75 percent, the main refinancing operations rate at 4.25 percent, and the marginal lending facility rate at 4.50 percent. ECB President Christine Lagarde stated that incoming data confirm a continued disinflationary path across the euro area, with headline inflation having declined from its 2022 peak of 10.6 percent to approximately 2.2 percent in the latest flash estimate.

The decision reflects a careful balancing act between supporting economic recovery and ensuring price stability over the medium term. Euro area GDP growth has been modest, expanding at 0.3 percent quarter-on-quarter in the second quarter, while unemployment held steady at a historic low of 6.4 percent. However, services inflation remains sticky at 4.3 percent, and wage growth continues to run above pre-pandemic averages, complicating the final mile of the disinflation process.

Market participants had widely anticipated the hold, with euro-denominated overnight index swap curves pricing in the first rate cut no earlier than the December 2024 meeting. The ECB's forward guidance emphasized a data-dependent approach, noting that future interest rate decisions will be based on the inflation outlook, underlying inflation dynamics, and the strength of monetary policy transmission.

In its updated macroeconomic projections, the ECB staff forecast headline inflation to average 2.5 percent in 2024, declining to 2.2 percent in 2025 and 1.9 percent in 2026. Real GDP growth is projected at 0.8 percent for 2024, rising to 1.3 percent in 2025 as household real incomes recover and export demand strengthens. The Governing Council reiterated its commitment to maintaining restrictive monetary policy for as long as necessary to return inflation sustainably to the two percent target.
